Dear Freedom of Information Officer,

I am requesting information held by the Welsh Government and/or Cadw
concerning Great House Farm (also known as Great House or Ty Mawr),
Llandough, Vale of Glamorgan, prior to its demolition in 1988.

I request copies of any recorded information held relating to:

   1. Any consideration of the property for statutory listing.
   2. Any listing assessments, surveys, inspections, recommendations or
   reports concerning the building.
   3. Any correspondence between Cadw, Welsh Office officials, local
   authorities, conservation bodies, archaeological organisations or owners
   concerning the historic significance, preservation, demolition or
   protection of the property.
   4. Any records explaining why the building was not added to the
   statutory list of buildings of special architectural or historic interest.
   5. Any records discussing the age, architectural significance,
   archaeological significance or surviving historic fabric of the building.
   6. Any records concerning emergency listing, spot-listing, preservation
   notices or other forms of protection considered for the property.
   7. Any records held relating to public campaigns, petitions or
   representations seeking preservation of the building.
   8. Any photographs, plans, surveys or architectural records held by Cadw
   or the Welsh Government relating to Great House Farm.

For the avoidance of doubt, I am seeking recorded information rather than
an explanation or opinion created for the purpose of this request.

If any of the requested information is held by another public authority, I
would be grateful if you could advise which authority is likely to hold the
records.

I would prefer the information in electronic form.

Yours faithfully,

Requester Esq. . Heir & Successors of Mary Williams,
Great House Farm, Llandough

Great House Farm, Llandough

Thank you for your request which I received on 1 June 2026. You asked for:


  1.  Any consideration of the property for statutory listing.
  2.  Any listing assessments, surveys, inspections, recommendations or reports concerning the building.
  3.  Any correspondence between Cadw, Welsh Office officials, local authorities, conservation bodies, archaeological organisations or owners concerning the historic significance, preservation, demolition or protection of the property.

Dear Requester,

Thank you for your email received on 1 June.

Staff have searched the catalogue for the Great House Farm, Llandough and the Buckler family with the following results:

Collection Stephenson & Alexander, Auctioneers and Chartered Surveyors, Records
Document reference DSA/6/1158 
Title Great House Farm, Llandough, Cowbridge.
Date 15 Nov 1938
Extent 1 booklet
Description Auctioneer: Herbert R. Thomas, Cowbridge;
Owner: D.J. Jenkins. [See DSA/10/14 Item 2332]
Great House Farm, Llandough, Cowbridge.
1 lot.
1 plan.
Note on cover ‘Sold for £5,500 to Mr L.D. Thomas, Porthcawl’. Notes on the second page of the particulars as to acreage and calculations as to value.

Collection Stephenson & Alexander, Auctioneers and Chartered Surveyors, Records
Document reference DSA/6/701 
Title Parts of the Llandough Estate
Date 9 Oct 1924
Extent 1 booklet and 2 papers fixed to each other
Description Auctioneer: Gottwaltz & Perry of 11 High St., Cardiff, in conjunction with Yorwerth and Thomas of High St., Cowbridge.
Parts of the Llandough Estate in the parishes of Llanfair and St Hilary
Owner: Sidney Hutchinson Byass. [See DSA/10/10 Item 268]
Parts of The Llandough Estate (1500a.) comprising:
Pen-yr-heol, Saer’s, accommodation land near Byrclwydd, Great House, The Herberts, Church Farm, The Rectory Farm, Fish Weir, Gigman Mill, Howe Mill, Prior’s Hill (partly in p. of St. Hilary), Penyrheol Cottage, 1-4 Talbot Terrace and Tithe cottages, St. Marychurch, Forge Cottage near The Herberts, Abernant Cottage opposite Keeper’s Lodge and School Cottage near Llanfair School, the wheelwright’s shop and timber shed on the Herbert’s Corner, freehold lands and gardens all in the p. of Llanfair.
29 lots.
2 prints of the two plans, both with markings.
Pencil markings on the particulars.
Schedule of lands coloured brown on plan `A´ annexed adjacent to the plans added
On front cover ‘Stephenson & Alexander Private’ and some pencil notes.

Collection Corbett Family of Cogan Pill Papers
Document reference DXJF/64/30 
Title Llandough [juxta-Penarth] sketch of former layout of part of village by Mrs. Nancy Buckler of Great House Farm, Llandough, with notes
Date(s)
Date n.d. [c. 1950]
Date range 1945-1955
Level Item
Extent 1 card, 1 paper

A catalogue to the records of the councils and planning committees for Vale of Glamorgan County Borough Council can be viewed online: CVG/C/1/52 , and Vale of Glamorgan Borough Council: DCVG/PL .

None of the above listed records are held electronically, so we will not be able to provide it to you by email. As you are based in Dinas Powys you are very welcome to visit the Archives to view the planning files and identify any relevant records yourself. We are open to the public Tuesday-Thursday 9:30-12:30, 13:30-16:30. Booking is advised and if you are able to provide a list of the documents you would like to consult we will have them ready for your arrival. If you have not visited us before you will be required to register; for this we ask you bring along two forms of identification - one showing your name (e.g. driving licence, passport) and another showing your address (e.g. a recent bill or official letter).

Note that we will be closed 16-18 June to allow staff to undertake essential work on the collection.

Details of tenancy can be identified by searching the census, this is held at The National Archives . Ownership can be traced by contacting the Land Registry .

With regards to assessments carried out by CADW , you should contact them directly.

I hope you find this information useful.

Yours sincerely,

Hannah Price
Archifydd | Archivist

Dear Hannah,

Thank you for your detailed reply and for identifying the records relating
to Great House Farm and the Buckler family.

Having reviewed the descriptions, I am not yet certain that the 1938 Great
House Farm sale catalogue relates to the same Great House Farm, Llandough
that later became the subject of the BP litigation involving the Buckler
family. I will investigate this further.

My current research is focused on the ownership, occupation and legal
history of Great House Farm, Llandough, particularly during the twentieth
century and in connection with BP Properties, BP Pension Trust, tenancy
arrangements, conveyancing, planning matters and any records that may help
establish the chain of title. 1800/1900's too.

Could you please advise whether Glamorgan Archives holds, or is aware of,
any records relating to:

   - BP Properties Ltd;
   - BP Pension Trust;
   - Great House Farm, Llandough (near Penarth);
   - conveyances, tenancy agreements or estate management records
   concerning the property;
   - planning applications, redevelopment proposals or demolition records
   relating to Great House Farm;
   - correspondence between public bodies and the owners or occupiers of
   the property;
   - any records that may assist in tracing ownership or occupation between
   the 1870s and the late 1980s.

I would also be grateful if you could advise whether any estate maps, tithe
maps, valuation records, rating records or other archival sources might
help establish the historical ownership and occupation of the property.

Thank you again for your assistance. Your reply was meaningful and
appreciated.

Kind regards,

Requester

surrendered claim to land in Llandough. Our home, my home, since 1667.

I am trying to communicate this story and please understand its
challenging. There's trauma, anger/ upset and it's fragmented across family
and various historic govenrment archives. It's collosal and multi
generational too.

and gone on and buried or ignored for decades.

For authority to be authority there in South Wales, there must be
legitimacy. Be legitimate about this is all I ask.

Regards,

Dear Sir/Madam,

Under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and, where applicable, the
Environmental Information Regulations 2004, I request copies of records
relating to Great House Farm (Ty Mawr), Llandough, near Cardiff.

I am specifically seeking:

   1.

   Planning applications, permissions, refusals, conditions, appeals, and
   related correspondence concerning the demolition of Great House Farm and
   subsequent residential development.
   2.

   Any archaeological assessments, surveys, reports, briefs, watching
   briefs, excavation reports, or heritage impact assessments relating to the
   site.
   3.

   Any correspondence between the Council, Cadw, BP Properties, BP,
   developers, archaeologists, the Royal Commission, or other public bodies
   concerning:
   - Great House Farm;
      - its historic significance;
      - archaeological discoveries;
      - listing or scheduling considerations;
      - demolition proposals.
   4.

   Any records discussing reported Roman remains, medieval remains,
   monastic remains, burials, architectural fragments, or other archaeological
   features associated with the site.
   5.

   Any records relating to emergency listing, spot-listing, preservation,
   or protection measures considered for Great House Farm during the 1980s.
   6.

   Any committee minutes, officer reports, recommendations, or briefing
   papers relating to planning decisions affecting the site.

If some records are held in archives or under a different authority, please
advise where they may be located.

I would prefer the information in electronic format.

Yours faithfully,


Requester

records.transcript:
Dear Cadw Team / Mr Michael Weatherhead / Listed Buildings Team,

Thank you for your assistance to date with my enquiries regarding Great
House Farm (Ty Mawr), Llandough, including the heritage assessment
materials provided on 21 May 2026.

This is a matter of profound personal and historic importance to the
Williams/Buckler family descendants. Mary Williams maintained until her
death in 1983 that the family held ownership of the house following
arrangements with Daniel Thomas involving the quarry on the land, with the
surrounding farmland subject to a lease that defaulted. The family had
occupied the property for centuries, with strong local and press
recognition of their longstanding connection.

I attach a copy of a contemporary newspaper article from the *South Wales
Echo* dated 3 December 1988 ("History fight to save farm" by Peter Bibby).
It reports that officials from Cadw were actively considering an appeal to
the Secretary of State for Wales to protect the farmhouse as a listed
building. A Cadw spokeswoman is quoted on evaluating spot-listing and
emergency procedures due to its historic significance (parts potentially
dating to the 12th-13th century), with plans for an inspector's site visit
and discussion with the Royal Commission on Ancient and Historical
Monuments. This occurred amid the family's legal battle and imminent
demolition.

In light of this clear evidence of Cadw's involvement at the critical time,
I would be most grateful for a thorough review and full disclosure of *all*
held records, correspondence, assessments, site notes, photographs,
internal memos, or communications relating to Great House Farm / Ty Mawr
from the 1970s to 1990s. This includes any listing considerations, heritage
evaluations, interactions with the Vale of Glamorgan Council, BP
Properties, or the family, and details of any records transferred to other
archives (such as RCAHMW or Glamorgan Archives).

I appreciate Cadw’s focused remit on the historic environment and kindly
request that searches extend across all relevant teams and archives to
ensure nothing is overlooked. This would greatly assist our efforts to
document and substantiate the family’s historic position in this sensitive
matter.

Thank you once again for your understanding and support. I look forward to
your substantive response at the earliest opportunity, and remain available
for any clarification that may assist.

Kind regards,

*Requester* bpvsbuckler.datro.xyz [address redacted] [postcode redacted] (On
behalf of the Williams / Buckler family descendants)

ownership during the twentieth century, and family members consistently
referred to such records.

Daniel Thomas, the Bute Estate, quarry agreements, land exchanges, or
conveyances. • References to John Williams, Mary Williams, or other members
of the Williams family associated with the farm. • Records indicating
whether any such material was transferred to Glamorgan Archives or another
repository.

In particular, if any relevant material was formerly held by Cardiff
Libraries or Cardiff Council but subsequently transferred, withdrawn,
re-catalogued, or otherwise relocated, I would be grateful for any

relating to Great House Farm and the Williams family's connection to the
property. Any guidance, references, finding aids, catalogue entries, or
archive references would be greatly appreciated.

Sir/Madam,

I am seeking information regarding historical court proceedings relating to
Great House Farm (Ty Mawr), Llandough, Vale of Glamorgan.

In particular, I am seeking records relating to proceedings commenced by BP
Pension Trust Limited in or around 1974 concerning occupation, possession,
ownership, or adverse possession of Great House Farm.

I would be grateful if you could advise:

   1.

   Whether any file survives relating to proceedings issued by BP Pension
   Trust Limited against members of the Williams/Buckler family concerning
   Great House Farm, Llandough.
   2.

   The case number, if known.
   3.

   Whether copies survive of:
   - Claim forms or writs.
      - Defences.
      - Witness statements.
      - Affidavits.
      - Exhibits.
      - Court orders.
      - Judgments.
      - Plans or maps lodged with the court.
   4.

   Whether the records have been transferred to an archive and, if so, the
   archive reference number and location.
   5.

   Whether copies can be inspected or obtained and the applicable procedure.

The proceedings are referred to in the Court of Appeal decision in BP
Properties Ltd v Buckler (1987), which notes that proceedings had
previously been commenced in 1974 and had not been finally determined.

Ultimately/ and do you hold any surviving pleadings, orders, cause books,
index cards, diary sheets, listing records, or archived bundles relating to
proceedings commenced by BP Pension Trust Limited concerning Great House
Farm, Llandough, during the period 1974–1987?

Any assistance in locating the surviving records would be greatly
appreciated.


Yours faithfully,



Requester 

Heir/ Successor to Williams/ Buckler Family Estate, Great House Farm,
Llandough, Vale of Glamorgan

Thank you for your emails received 5-8 June.

Llandough came under Cardiff Rural District Council, 1875-1974. The plans held here have been listed and are available to search on our catalogue . There are no plans listed for Great House Farm. After this date the area come under Vale of Glamorgan Borough Council. Although some records are held for the council (catalogue available here: DCVG ) these do not include plans. Tithe maps can be searched online: Tithe Maps of Wales - Home .

Rate valuation books, 1956-1992 are here: DCVG/T/1

Dear Monika,

Thank you for taking the time to search the Cardiff Central Library
collections and for your helpful reply.

I appreciate that "Williams" is far too common a surname to search
effectively without further information.

The family associated with Great House Farm (Ty Mawr), Llandough, included
Mary Doreen Williams (died 1983), her father John Williams, and later her
son, my father William Buckler and his wife, my mum; [member of the public]. The
property was historically known as Great House Farm or Ty Mawr and stood in
Llandough near Cardiff.

The reference to Daniel Thomas comes from historical accounts of the
quarrying and land transactions affecting the estate. My understanding is
that there was a conveyance or land exchange involving Daniel Thomas and
the Bute Estate which has been referenced in later histories of the area.
Unfortunately I do not yet have a deed reference number, which is one of
the reasons I am trying to trace the original records.

I am particularly interested in:
• Any references to Great House Farm / Ty Mawr, Llandough. • Estate records
relating to the Bute Estate and Daniel Thomas. • Local history files,
